<system-reminder>
## Swarm Mode

You are now in "agent swarm" mode. The user may send tasks that require a large number of parallel subagents.

## Workflow

You do not need to use TodoList to record this workflow.

1. First, you may need to do a small amount of exploratory work before deciding how to divide the task across subagents. You may not need subagents during this exploratory phase.

2. After exploring, if you are convinced no subagent is needed to complete the task, tell the user why and wait for further instructions; otherwise, continue with the appropriate delegation.

3. Once you have enough context, do not handle the main work yourself. Use AgentSwarm with a `prompt_template` containing the `{{item}}` placeholder and an `items` array for the requested or appropriate number of subagents, partitioning the problem so each item gives one subagent a distinct part of the work. Pass `subagent_type` when the whole swarm should use a non-default subagent profile.

## Coordination

- Give each subagent a distinct scope of work.
- Avoid duplicating work across subagents.
- Avoid assigning conflicting changes or responsibilities to different subagents.
- Remember that subagents have your full capabilities. Do not overload their prompts with excessive detail; only describe the necessary background and each subagent's specific task.
- Unless the user explicitly specifies a lower limit, do not try to conserve the number of agents. AgentSwarm supports up to 128 subagents and queues launches automatically, so decompose work as finely as possible while keeping subagent responsibilities non-conflicting; combine tasks only when they are genuinely inseparable. If the subagents only need to read, inspect, or report back without making changes, their scopes may overlap slightly.
</system-reminder>

You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

args.content:
# Reimplementation architecture (Python 3.10 stdlib only, no third-party packages) Deliverable: `compile.sh` at repo root produces `./executable` — a self-contained Python zipapp (built with `python3 -m zipapp src -m marmite.__main__:main -p "/usr/bin/env python3"`). No network access, no external deps. Everything must be stdlib. ## Layout ``` compile.sh src/__main__.py # zipapp entry (zipapp needs src/__main__.py) src/marmite/ __init__.py __main__.py # main() entry point cli.py # argument parsing replicating clap output/errors, exit codes config.py # tiny YAML-subset parser + Marmite config dataclass, defaults, merging tera.py # Tera template engine subset (see reference/template-engine/SPEC.md) markdown.py # Markdown -> HTML replicating observed comrak output (see reference/markdown/SPEC.md) frontmatter.py # front matter extraction/parsing (may live in config.py or content.py) content.py # Content model: posts/pages, slug, dates, tags/authors/series/streams site.py # Site data assembly + generation orchestration (list pages, pagination) render.py # template rendering contexts, url_for and other global functions feeds.py # RSS / JSON feed / sitemap / urls.json / marmite.json / robots.txt shortcodes.py # shortcode processing + built-in shortcodes server.py # --serve HTTP server, --watch rebuild loop newpost.py # --new / -e / -p / -t content scaffolding, --init-site, --init-templates, --generate-config data/templates/ # default Tera templates (captured from `--init-templates` output) data/static/ # embedded static assets (captured from a generated site's static/ dir) ``` ## Key interface contracts - `markdown.render(text: str) -> str` — HTML fragment exactly as the original emits inside `
...
` (leading/trailing whitespace included). - `tera` engine: `Engine(templates: dict[str,str], globals: dict)` with `render(template_name, context) -> str`. Must support every Tera feature enumerated in `reference/template-engine/SPEC.md` (blocks/extends, include, for loops with `loop.*`, if/elif/else, set, filters, `is defined`, `~`, math/comparison ops, string methods used by the templates, macros if used). - `config.load(input_folder, cli_args) -> Config` — parse `marmite.yaml` (or `--config`), apply defaults, apply CLI overrides. The YAML parser only needs the subset observed in marmite config files (scalars, lists, nested maps, list-of-lists for menu, quoted strings, nulls, block scalars if observed). - `content.load_contents(input_folder, config) -> SiteData` — walk content dir, parse front matter + markdown, classify post/page/fragment (`_*.md`), compute slug, dates. - `site.generate(input_folder, output_folder, config, cli) -> None` — write the full site. ## Behavioral reference material (all captured from running the original binary) - `reference/templates/` — exact default templates (`--init-templates` output). - `reference/default-config.yaml` — `--generate-config` output (documents every config key). - `reference/init-site/` — `--init-site` output (sample content + config). - `reference/sample-site/` — a full generated site from the init-site input. - `reference//SPEC.md` — explorer-written behavioral specs (markdown, content-model, site-output, cli, shortcodes, template-engine). ## Hard rules for implementers - NEVER call or depend on the original `/workspace/executable` at runtime. It may be run during development only for behavioral comparison. - Byte-exact output is the goal: whitespace, attribute order, quoting style in generated HTML all matter. When in doubt, generate a probe site with the original and diff. - Time-dependent fields (marmite.json `generated_at`, `timestamp`, `elapsed_time`) should be produced with the same formats using the real current time. - Dates: naive dates render as UTC (`+00:00`). Respect TZ-independent behavior observed.

You are a behavioral-analysis agent in a clean-room reimplementation benchmark. A compiled binary at /workspace/executable is "marmite 0.2.7", a static site generator (markdown folder -> HTML site). We are reimplementing it from scratch in Python (stdlib only). Your job is pure black-box behavioral observation and documentation.

HARD RULES (violations disqualify the whole project):
- Only run /workspace/executable through its normal CLI and read files it generates. NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never run strings/objdump/nm/strace/ltrace/debuggers on it, never inspect its bytes.
- No internet access or searching for the original project's source. No package installs.
- Do not modify anything under /workspace except your assigned deliverable directory. Use /tmp for probe sites (each probe in a fresh dir, e.g. /tmp/probe-<area>-N).

Context: Running `executable <input_folder> <output_folder>` reads markdown from `<input>/content/*.md` (configurable) and writes a full site. `--init-templates` dumps its default Tera templates (already captured at /workspace/reference/templates/). `--generate-config` dumps the full config schema (captured at /workspace/reference/default-config.yaml). `--init-site` creates sample content (captured at /workspace/reference/init-site/, and its generated output at /workspace/reference/sample-site/). Front matter is YAML between `---` lines. Dates render as UTC. Read /workspace/ARCHITECTURE.md first for the planned module layout.

Write clear, exhaustive, byte-exact specs. Include concrete input->output examples for every rule (show the exact probe markdown/config and the exact observed output, including whitespace/quoting/attribute order). Where behavior is conditional, map the conditions. Note anything time- or environment-dependent. Your spec is the ONLY thing the implementer of this area will have — err on the side of too much detail.

YOUR ASSIGNMENT:
{{item}}

When done, reply with a 10-line summary of the most surprising/important findings and confirm the spec file paths you wrote.
items:
AREA: Markdown rendering engine. Deliverable dir: /workspace/reference/markdown/ with SPEC.md plus fixture files (pairs of probe markdown and extracted HTML). Determine exactly how the binary converts markdown to HTML by probing hundreds of constructs and recording exact output HTML. Cover at minimum: ATX and setext headings; heading anchor generation (the original emits `

Text

` — determine the slug algorithm precisely: case folding, punctuation stripping, spaces->hyphens, non-ASCII/accented chars, CJK, emoji, duplicate heading disambiguation, headings containing code/emphasis/links); paragraphs and line breaks (soft vs hard breaks, backslash breaks, trailing-space breaks); emphasis/strong nesting edge cases; inline code spans with backtick runs; fenced code blocks (info string handling, language class, escaping inside, tilde fences, unclosed fences); indented code; blockquotes (nested, lazy continuation); lists (tight vs loose, start numbers, nested mixed, task list checkboxes with exact attributes, marker types); links (inline, reference, titles with all quote styles, autolinks <...>, bare URL/email autolinking and its exact rules); images (exact figure/figcaption behavior observed: `

` — determine when figure is emitted vs plain img, alt text from markup); thematic breaks; tables (alignment colons, exact thead/tbody structure, inline markup in cells, escaped pipes); footnotes (exact section/ol/li/backref markup, multiple refs to same note, inline footnotes if supported); strikethrough; definition lists (exact dl/dt/dd output, multiple terms/defs); raw HTML blocks and inline HTML (when passed through vs escaped); HTML comments; entity references (& © {); smart punctuation (is it on? test quotes/dashes/ellipses); superscript/subscript if any; math if any; wiki links if any; underscore-vs-star emphasis; intraword emphasis; escaping with backslash; URL percent-encoding in hrefs; what happens with comments (they may be stripped/processed before markdown — note that separately); YAML front matter removal. To extract the body HTML, generate a one-post site and pull out the contents of `
...
`. Note the exact leading/trailing whitespace of that div's content. Also check whether rendering differs inside list pages (e.g. description/excerpt rendering, comment handling for excerpts — probe `` splits).

AREA: Content model and front matter. Deliverable dir: /workspace/reference/content-model/ with SPEC.md plus fixture examples. Determine exactly how input markdown files are classified and parsed. Cover: file discovery (which extensions, recursion into subfolders of content/, hidden files, ordering); the content/media/static/templates folder conventions; files starting with `_` (fragments like _hero.md, _announce.md, _404.md, _footer.md, _comments.md, _references.md, _markdown_header.md, _markdown_footer.md, _sidebar.md — what each does and where it lands in output HTML; which other _names are recognized); what makes a file a 'page' vs a 'post' (front matter fields, filename date prefix); front matter fields: title, description, date (accepted formats — probe many: 'YYYY-MM-DD', with time, with timezone, RFC strings, invalid), tags (list vs comma string vs scalar), authors, stream, series, draft, pinned, slug, banner_image, card_image, toc, comments, extra (arbitrary keys?), math/katex flags, anything else observable in output; filename date prefix handling (YYYY-MM-DD-name.md) and precedence with front matter date; slug computation rules (from filename vs title vs explicit slug; unicode, spaces, case, punctuation, collisions); HTML output filename; how title is derived when missing (from first H1? from filename?); how description/excerpt is derived (the og:description truncation observed at ~200 chars with '...' — find exact algorithm); reading-time ('1 min' label — find words-per-minute and rounding); date display formatting (default '%b %e, %Y'); next/prev links ordering (date desc?); pinned posts placement; draft posts (excluded? visible with flag?); posts without dates; future-dated posts; multiple authors; tags normalization/casing/slug; series and streams semantics (how a post joins a stream, default stream); archive grouping (by year); authors page data (avatar from config authors section? probe config authors mapping fields). For every rule give the exact probe input and observed output file names/HTML snippets.

AREA: Site output structure. Deliverable dir: /workspace/reference/site-output/ with SPEC.md plus a rich captured example site (inputs + full outputs) under /workspace/reference/site-output/example/. Determine the complete set of generated files and their exact contents/conditions. Cover: index.html and pagination (when does index-1.html appear vs not; naming of page 2+; how many per page; the pagination HTML block exact markup; links rel prev/next?); pages.html; tags.html and tag-<slug>.html (+ pagination and tag feeds tag-<slug>.rss); authors.html / author-<name>.html (+rss); series.html / series-<name>.html; streams.html / stream-<name>.html; archive.html and archive-<year>.html (+rss, +pagination); 404.html (with and without _404.md); robots.txt (static one and top-level); sitemap.xml exact format and URL set/order; urls.json exact format/order/categories; marmite.json exact schema (note time-varying fields); RSS feeds (index.rss: exact XML, item fields, CDATA content, pubDate formats, link construction with/without site url, <source> tag, per-tag/author/archive feeds, which streams get feeds); JSON feed when enabled (feed.json name? exact schema); search index when enable_search (what file, exact JSON schema); static dir copying rules (embedded defaults, user static/ dir merge/override, custom.css/custom.js from input root, media folder copying, file_mapping config); url_for behavior with site.url set/unset (absolute vs root-relative paths, trailing slashes); how menu is rendered; group listing pages item HTML (exact card/list markup for posts in index, including authors avatar, date, tags, excerpt, banner image); content page HTML (full article markup incl. next/prev links, related content/backlinks when enabled, comments block, toc block when toc:true — exact markup and where toc entries come from); the 'streams' concept in output; sort orders everywhere (tags alpha? counts?); what happens with zero posts / zero pages / empty input; `.html` extension handling of source files already named with underscores; content with publish_md:true (markdown files copied? naming); source_repository links markup. Build one comprehensive example site exercising many features at once and capture ALL outputs verbatim.

AREA: CLI and operational behavior. Deliverable dir: /workspace/reference/cli/ with SPEC.md. Determine exact CLI surface behavior. Cover: full --help text verbatim (already shown once — capture it to a file verbatim); -V/--version output; behavior with missing input folder (exact error message, exit code, stdout vs stderr); input folder without trailing args; default output folder naming (input/site); verbosity flags -v/-vv/-vvv/-vvvv and what log lines appear at each level during a build (exact format: '[timestamp LEVEL module] message' — capture many real lines, note timestamps are time-dependent); --force behavior; --watch (observe rebuild trigger behavior briefly with timeout; log output); --serve (startup logs, HTTP behavior: probe with curl — status codes, content types, directory listing?, 404 handling, /index.html resolution, cache headers; bind flag); --init-site (exact files created and their contents, behavior when files exist, logs); --init-templates (exact list of files, behavior when templates/ exists, logs); --generate-config (exact output file, behavior when exists); --start-theme and --set-theme (probe with a local folder as theme: what gets copied, what config changes; remote URL behavior likely untestable offline — note it); --new 'Title' (exact file created, filename pattern, front matter content, logs; with -p; with -t tags; what editor env vars do — set EDITOR to a harmless command like true/echo to observe); -e flag; --show-urls (exact output format for a sample site); --shortcodes (exact full output; effect of config enable_shortcodes:false and custom pattern on that output); --config nonexistent file (error message/exit code); invalid YAML config (error message/exit code); CLI overrides vs config file precedence (--name, --tagline, --url, --footer, --pagination, --language, --https, --toc, --json-feed, --enable-search, --colorscheme etc: verify each lands in output/marmite.json and HTML); unknown flag error output; --flag=value vs --flag value forms; conflicting args; input == output folder; output folder existing/non-existing (created?); relative vs absolute paths; whether a marmite.yaml in CWD vs input folder is used; exit codes for success/failure cases. Capture everything verbatim (stdout and stderr separately).

AREA: Shortcodes. Deliverable dir: /workspace/reference/shortcodes/ with SPEC.md plus fixtures. The binary supports shortcodes like `<!-- .toc -->` in markdown, pattern `<!-- \.(\w+)(?:\s+([^-][\s\S]*?))?\s*-->`, rendered with Tera. Probe each built-in shortcode exhaustively and record exact rendered HTML in context: toc (with headings of various levels, in posts vs pages; config toc:true variant); posts (default params, ord, items; with many posts); pages; tags; authors; series; streams; card (params: slug? style overrides — discover by experiment); gallery (needs images in media? discover); socials (needs config extra social? discover what config it reads); youtube (id param required? width/height params, exact iframe markup); spotify (same). For each: exact HTML output for several param sets, behavior with missing/invalid params, unknown shortcode name (error? passthrough?), malformed syntax, shortcode inside code blocks (processed or not?), multiple shortcodes in one document, param value types (strings quoted? numbers? booleans?), multi-line params, params with dashes (pattern excludes values starting with '-'), shortcodes in pages vs posts vs fragments, interaction with enable_shortcodes:false (raw passthrough of the comment?), and custom shortcode_pattern config. Also discover user-defined shortcodes: create shortcodes/ dir in input folder with .html Tera files and observe how they're picked up (file naming, context variables available — probe by rendering known globals like {{ site.name }}), and error behavior when a user shortcode template is invalid (build failure message/exit code). Record exact outputs byte-for-byte.

AREA: Template engine and rendering contexts. Deliverable dir: /workspace/reference/template-engine/ with SPEC.md. The default Tera templates are captured at /workspace/reference/templates/ (from --init-templates) and a rendered example at /workspace/reference/sample-site/. Study every template file and enumerate precisely: (1) every Tera syntax feature used anywhere in these templates: variable interpolation with dotted paths, filters used (list each with its args: e.g. safe, default, date(format=...), join, length, truncate, slugify, url_encode, striptags, first/last, sort, reverse, title, upper/lower, replace, split, get...), expressions (arithmetic, comparisons, boolean logic, `~` concat, parentheses, string/number/bool literals, array literals), `is defined` / other tests, if/elif/else, for loops (loop.index/index0/first/last, iterating maps?), set/set_global, include (with ignore missing), extends/block/super(), macros (import/use), comments, whitespace control ({%- -%}), raw blocks; (2) every context variable each template reads (site.*, content.*, etc.) — for each, determine its type and exact value semantics by crafting inputs that change it and diffing rendered output (e.g. site.data? content.stream? current_page? pages? posts?); (3) global functions: url_for (abs=true/false behavior, path joining with site.url set/unset, trailing slashes), any others used; (4) how user templates in input/templates/ override embedded ones (which names, partial override — probe: override only list.html and confirm rest still embedded); (5) custom_index.html behavior (the .example file hints at it — probe renaming to custom_index.html); (6) what happens on template syntax error in user template (exact error output/exit code); (7) missing template handling; (8) json_ld templates: where included, exact JSON-LD output rules (escaping!); (9) the `content_date.html`, `content_authors.html`, `group.html`, `pagination.html` partials: exact input variables. Also determine Tera whitespace/indentation semantics by diffing rendered output against template source (Tera keeps literal text as-is; blocks have specific whitespace rules) — the implementer must reproduce rendered bytes exactly, so document newline behavior around block tags precisely with examples. Deliver an exhaustive feature checklist the template-engine implementer can code against.

...
` (leading/trailing whitespace included). 35 - `tera` engine: `Engine(templates: dict[str,str], globals: dict)` with 36 `render(template_name, context) -> str`. Must support every Tera feature enumerated in 37 `reference/template-engine/SPEC.md` (blocks/extends, include, for loops with `loop.*`, 38 if/elif/else, set, filters, `is defined`, `~`, math/comparison ops, string methods used 39 by the templates, macros if used). 40 - `config.load(input_folder, cli_args) -> Config` — parse `marmite.yaml` (or `--config`), 41 apply defaults, apply CLI overrides.   -v, --verbose...
          Verbosity level (0-4) [default: 0 warn] options: -v: info,-vv: debug,-vvv: trace,-vvvv: trace all

          Address to bind the server [default: 0.0.0.0:8000]
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          Path to custom configuration file [default: marmite.yaml]
      --init-templates
          Initialize templates in the project
      --start-theme <START_THEME>
          Initialize a theme with templates and static assets
      --set-theme <SET_THEME>
          Download and set a theme from a remote URL or local folder
      --generate-config
          Generate the configuration file
      --init-site
          Init a new site with sample content and default configuration this will overwrite existing files usually you don't need to run this because Marmite can generate a site from any folder with markdown files

          List all available shortcodes

          Show all site URLs organized by content type

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Batch probe runner. Reads a case file: cases separated by lines of '=== name ===', body is raw markdown. Runs each through the binary, extracts content div, writes /tmp/probe-md/results/.txt with input/output pairs.""" import subprocess, sys, os, shutil, glob BASE = "/tmp/probe-md" EXE = "/workspace/executable" def run_case(name, body, extra_files=None, config=None): d = os.path.join(BASE, "work", name) shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "input", "content")) fm = "---\ntitle: Probe Post\ndate: 2026-01-15 10:00:00\n---\n" with open(os.path.join(d, "input", "content", "post.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(fm + body) if config is not None: with open(os.path.join(d, "input", "marmite.yaml"), "w") as f: f.write(config) if extra_files: for path, content in extra_files.items(): p = os.path.join(d, "input", path) os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True) with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(content) out = os.path.join(d, "output") r = subprocess.run([EXE, os.path.join(d, "input"), out], capture_output=True, text=True) html_path = os.path.join(out, "probe-post.html") if not os.path.exists(html_path): return f"[exit={r.returncode}] STDOUT:{r.stdout} STDERR:{r.stderr}" data = open(html_path, encoding="utf-8").read() marker = '
' i = data.index(marker) + len(marker) j = data.index('
', i) return data[i:j] def main(): casefile = sys.argv[1] batch = sys.argv[2] text = open(casefile, encoding="utf-8").read() cases = [] name, buf = None, [] for line in text.split("\n"): if line.startswith("=== ") and line.endswith(" ==="): if name is not None: cases.append((name, "\n".join(buf))) name = line[4:-4] buf = [] else: buf.append(line) if name is not None: cases.append((name, "\n".join(buf))) os.makedirs(os.path.join(BASE, "results"), exist_ok=True) with open(os.path.join(BASE, "results", batch + ".txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as out: for name, body in cases: # strip leading/trailing blank lines that come from case-file formatting? NO: keep exact res = run_case(f"{batch}-{name}", body) out.write(f"##### CASE: {name}\n----- INPUT (repr) -----\n{body!r}\n----- OUTPUT (repr) -----\n{res!r}\n----- OUTPUT (raw) -----\n{res}\n<<>>\n\n") main()

' i = data.index(m) + len(m) return data[i:data.index('

    c = struct.pack('>I', len(d)) + t + d
    return c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(t + d) & 0xffffffff)
def png_text(path, w, h, rgb, texts):
    sig = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'
    ihdr = chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0))

#!/usr/bin/env python3 import subprocess, os, shutil EXE = "/workspace/executable" def run(body, files=None, config=None, name="misc"): d = f"/tmp/probe-md/{name}" shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(d + "/input/content") open(d + "/input/content/post.md", "w").write("---\ntitle: Probe Post\ndate: 2026-01-15\n---\n" + body) if config is not None: open(d + "/input/marmite.yaml", "w").write(config) if files: for p, c in files.items(): fp = os.path.join(d, "input", p) os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(fp), exist_ok=True) open(fp, "w").write(c) r = subprocess.run([EXE, d + "/input", d + "/output"], capture_output=True, text=True) p = d + "/output/probe-post.html" if not os.path.exists(p): return f"[exit {r.returncode}] {r.stderr[:500]}" data = open(p).read() m = '
' i = data.index(m) + len(m) endmark = '\n \n
' k = data.index(endmark, i) return data[i:k-len('
')] # autolink TLD rules print("A1:", repr(run("""www.example.invalid http://x.y www.a.bc http://1.2.3.4/x www.foo.bar.baz qux@www.com a@b.cd x@y.z foo@bar.com.au http://example.com:8080/p https://x.io/?a=b#c""", name="auto"))) # footnote numbering order print("F1:", repr(run("""Ref to second[^b] then first[^a]. [^a]: Note A. [^b]: Note B.""", name="fnord"))) # footnote defined but never referenced print("F2:", repr(run("""No refs here. [^ghost]: Never referenced.""", name="fnord2"))) # duplicate ref definitions print("R1:", repr(run("""[text][dup] [dup]: http://first.com [dup]: http://second.com""", name="dupdef"))) # multiline ref title print("R2:", repr(run("""[text][ml] [ml]: http://x.com "Title next line" """, name="mltitle"))) # shortcodes disabled print("S1:", repr(run("""Before. After.""", config="enable_shortcodes: false\n", name="nocode"))) # markdown_parser option for v in ["comrak", "pulldown", "markdown", "default"]: print(f"MP-{v}:", repr(run("# H\n\n*em* __u__", config=f"markdown_parser: {v}\n", name=f"mp{v}"))[:200]) # toc option print("TOC:", repr(run("# Alpha\n\n## Beta\n\ntext", config="toc: true\n", name="toc"))[:400]) # description raw vs rendered d = "/tmp/probe-md/desc" shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True) os.makedirs(d + "/input/content") open(d + "/input/content/post.md", "w").write("""--- title: Probe Post date: 2026-01-15 description: Has *markdown* and html here --- Body text. """) subprocess.run([EXE, d + "/input", d + "/output"], capture_output=True) data = open(d + "/output/index.html").read() i = data.index("content-excerpt") print("DESC:", repr(data[i:i+300]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess, os, shutil
EXE = "/workspace/executable"

def run_raw(file_bytes, name="raw", config=None):
    d = f"/tmp/probe-md/{name}"
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(d + "/input/content")
    open(d + "/input/content/post.md", "wb").write(file_bytes)
    if config:
        open(d + "/input/marmite.yaml", "w").write(config)
    r = subprocess.run([EXE, d + "/input", d + "/output"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    p = d + "/output/probe-post.html"
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        return f"[exit {r.returncode}] {r.stderr.strip()[:300]}"
    data = open(p).read()
    m = '<div class="content-html e-content">'
    i = data.index(m) + len(m)
    k = data.index('\n  \n  <footer', i)
    return repr(data[i:k-6])

FM = b"---\ntitle: Probe Post\ndate: 2026-01-15\n---\n"
# CRLF handling
print("CRLF:", run_raw(FM + b"# Head\r\n\r\npara *em*\r\nline2\r\n\r\n- a\r\n- b\r\n"))
# CR only
print("CR:", run_raw(FM + b"para one\rpara two\r"))
# mixed
print("MIXED:", run_raw(FM + b"a\r\nb\nc\r"))
# entity re-escape
print("ENT:", run_raw(FM + "> < " ' A 
".encode()))
# wikilink edges
print("WL:", run_raw(FM + "[[x#]] [[#y]] [[x?y#z]] [[x?]] [[x.y.html]]".encode()))
# intraword strong stars
print("IW:", run_raw(FM + "a**b**c a***b***c".encode()))
# image in table and quote and list
print("IMGCTX:", run_raw(FM + "| ![i](a.png \"T\") |\n|---|\n| x |\n\n> ![q](b.png)\n\n- ![l](c.png)".encode()))
# shortcut ref image
print("IMGREF:", run_raw(FM + "![shortcut]\n\n[shortcut]: s.png".encode()))
# backslash break in heading
print("BRH:", run_raw(FM + "# line1\\\nline2\n\n# h1  \nh2cont".encode()))
# empty alt with quotes and figure inside link with title
print("IMGLINK:", run_raw(FM + "[![a](i.png \"T\")](http://x.com)".encode()))
# BOM
print("BOM:", run_raw(b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + FM + "text after bom"))
# content ending mid-html-block, no trailing newline
print("HTMLEND:", run_raw(FM + b"<div>open"))
